latest_rss.title: The heart of governance: Sharing the people's joys and sorrows
latest_rss.summary: "He who delights in what the people delight in, the people will also delight in his joys; he who grieves over what grieves the people, the people will also grieve over his sorrows." This line from Mencius speaks to a profound emotional resonance between those who govern and those they serve. In essence, governance is not cold management – it is empathy, heart meeting heart.This ancient teaching offers a sharp mirror for today's governance. Whether a policy succeeds often depends less on how meticulously it is drafted than on whether the people truly embrace it. Decisions made behind closed doors, far removed from daily realities, will inevitably fall flat – no matter how well-intentioned. But when officials walk the fields, listen to grievances in the alleys, and turn public complaints into actionable priorities, governance becomes grounded and credible.This rings especially true in cultural welfare. Among independents who did not support any particular political party, 54% favored more dialogue.
